data.text/markdown: 2. The Data

The data was generated using make_data.py and saved as seven CSV files in the data folder. I generated 50 loyalty members, 25 products, 10 options, 1,200 orders, 2,377 order lines, 2,064 line options and 1,515 payments. The data covers the 12-month period ending November 1, 2026. I used a fixed random seed of 6301 so the same data is generated each time. I intentionally made the payment totals for Orders 1 and 2 incorrect by adding $1.00 to each. I will check for these differences using SQL in Part B.

data.text/markdown: Initially, my data showed orders spread almost evenly throughout the day, which did not seem realistic for a campus café. I changed the order generation in make_data.py to make mornings and lunchtime busier. The updated chart now shows the highest number of orders around 9 AM and another busy period between 12 PM and 1 PM, with fewer orders later in the afternoon. This seems more realistic for a café serving students.## Summary By adjusting the order generation logic to weight morning and lunchtime hours more heavily, the synthetic data now reflects realistic café traffic patterns. This makes the dashboard more useful for identifying true peak hours, which could help with staffing decisions or inventory planning in a real-world scenario.

data.text/markdown: Section 6: Answers You Already Knew

I generated the data using make_data.py, so I already know the answers to these three questions before running the SQL queries. How many loyalty members are there? I expect 50 because my script generated 50 members. How many products are on the menu? I expect 25 because I included 25 menu items. How many orders were generated? I expect 1,200 because my script created 1,200 orders.

data.text/markdown: I created a view called product_sales to track how many units of each product were sold and the revenue generated, excluding add-ons. Espresso had the highest product revenue at $1,268.76, followed by Brownie at $1,242.15. The café can use this view regularly to see which products are generating the most sales without rewriting the SQL query.
